stem:

How many ions are produced from the complex \(\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6\text{Cl}_2\) in solution?
_note: The book labels the alternatives (i)-(iv); mapped positionally to A-D. Derived: the six \(\text{NH}_3\) groups are inside the coordination sphere, so \([\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_2\) ionises to one \([\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{2+}\) cation and two \(\text{Cl}^-\) ions = 3 ions.

stem:
Amongst the following ions which one has the highest magnetic moment value?

(i) \([\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}\)

(ii) \([\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}\)

(iii) \([\text{Zn}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}\)
_note: The book prints only THREE alternatives for this question, not four. Shipped as free-response with the three printed choices kept in the stem rather than inventing a fourth option — the MCQ core requires exactly A,B,C,D.

_note: The book labels the alternatives (i)-(iv); mapped positionally to A-D. Derived: oxalate is the only didentate ligand here, so the trisoxalato entity is the only chelate — three five-membered rings — and the chelate effect makes it the most stable of the four.
